title: I Let the Dentist Office Keep the Double-Book Policy

parts.text: I checked in at 8:00 and the chair was already full. I am twenty-seven, receptionist who also gets cleanings here, which is awkward. The office manager, Vicky, double-booked hygienists to 'maximize.' The waiting room magazines were all from 2019, a specific Golf Digest. My patient, Mr. Alvarez, had taken the bus. The polish paste smelled like fake mint. Vicky said, "Just say we're running a little behind" I said, "We're double-booked. I can say that" Vicky wanted me to tell him to wait forty minutes without the truth. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted. A vending machine hummed in another room like a bored insect, which fit i. I counted three ceiling tiles with water stains before I spoke again. My socks had a hole I had been ignoring since Tuesday, which fit i.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: She wants a soft lie, and Mr. Alvarez is watching the clock over the fish tank.

parts.text: I told Mr. Alvarez we double-booked and offered to reschedule with a discount on paste. He laughed, surprisingly kind. Vicky hissed in the hall. The hygienist, Jen, who hates the policy, squeezed my shoulder. Corporate mystery-shopped the next week and asked patients about wait times. Mr. Alvarez told the truth too. Double-booking paused. Golf Digest stayed. I still work the desk. The fish tank gurgles like it knows. Maximizing is a word that should not apply to gums. Jen said, "Thank you for saying it" Vicky said, "You made us look unprofessional" Jen brought real mints from the grocery, not paste. We hid them from Vicky like teenagers.
